newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Opp'n warns against media reforms.
newsitem.headline: Australian Opp'n warns against media reforms.

text.p: Australian government plans to ease media ownership laws would reduce diversity and were aimed at helping the country's richest man, Labor opposition leader Kim Beazley said on Thursday.
"There's nothing on the table from this government which will advance media diversity, only contract it," Beazley told reporters.

Newspapers on Thursday reported that tough media ownership limits may be eased, allowing media tycoons Kerry Packer and Rupert Murdoch to expand their empires and foreigners to take bigger media stakes.
Communications Minister Richard Alston declined to comment.
"I'm not confirming or denying anything," he told reporters. Alston said the government was still considering the issue and would announce its decision "when it's appropriate".

According to newspaper reports, the plan would allow a single operator to own one newspaper and one television station in the major cities of Sydney and Melbourne and would raise foreign ownership limits.
It would clear the way for Packer, Australia's richest man, to take over newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd and for Murdoch's News Corp to increase its shareholding in the Seven Network Ltd.
"Well, quite clearly the intention of the government is to benefit him (Packer)," Beazley said when asked if the changes were aimed at helping Packer.
Beazley urged the government not to change current rules.
The conservative Liberal-National government is reviewing rules set by the former Labor government limiting cross-media ownership in newspapers and television stations in major markets to 15 percent.
